clue.text: Empty nest and no memories — bad time for OAP?

indicators.note: bad suggests letters gone wrong, so the pooled letters are rearranged
an empty nest keeps only its shell, the first and last letters of the word nest

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly couple whose children have left home and who can remember nothing: a bad time for a pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves NT from 'nest'; 'bad' shuffles NT with NOMEMORIES. The question mark marks the definition as an example: OAP is an old-age pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: A forgetful lapse is jokingly blamed on age, so it is a typical episode for an elderly person.

clue.text: Joyce's alter ego, in phase with male name ("boy raised in God")

parts.note: a step is a stage or phase in a process
he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: the boy sits in God, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: Deus is Latin for God

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A note on James Joyce's fictional self, apparently in tune with a man's name explained in parentheses.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' before 'phase' is only a link word; the second 'in' does the inserting, and 'raised' turns the boy upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce's hero of A Portrait of the Artist and Ulysses is widely read as the author's fictional self.

clue.text: Writing up article about show in African capital

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other
in a down clue writing a word up means setting it upwards, back to front

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
to air something is to show it in public

explanation.surface: Someone writes up a piece about an exhibition held in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: NA (AN written upwards) goes about AIR. 'Capital' looks like a city but means money.
explanation.definitionFit: The naira is the currency of Nigeria, and capital can mean money as well as a chief city.

clue.text: Having prolonged good luck, film here once?

definitions.meaning: before digital cameras, photographic film came wound on a spool

explanation.surface: A lucky streak, and a playful nod to where photographic film used to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler on a winning streak is said to be riding a lucky run; old camera film was literally wound on a spool.

clue.text: See 1
Kiss one of two kissers wearing very large bloomers

indicators.note: the outer piece wears the inner one like clothing, so it goes around it

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size for very large people
X is the cross for a kiss at the end of a letter
a lip is one of the two parts of the mouth that kiss

explanation.surface: A kiss on the lips from someone wearing outsize knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like underwear but means flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that bloom can be called bloomers, and the oxlip is a yellow-flowered primula.

clue.text: Woman with adopted youngster eating a Mexican dish

indicators.note: a woman who has adopted a child takes it in, so it goes inside her name

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name

indicators.note: the youngster eats the a, so it goes inside

parts.note: a child is a youngster

explanation.surface: A woman and her adopted child eat a Mexican meal together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating' puts the A inside the youngster first; 'adopted' then takes that whole group inside the woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rolled tortilla with a filling and chilli sauce, a classic dish of Mexico.

clue.text: Reticently, I log off site that's educational

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone quietly logs off a learning website.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges RETICENTLYILOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of learning, such as the colleges of that name in Cambridge, Oxford and Dublin, is an educational site.

clue.text: Fantastically fine and super, so extremely delightful?

definitions.text: Fantastically fine and super, so extremely delightful?

indicators.note: fantastically means wildly, so the pooled letters are rearranged
the extremes of the word delightful are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something so fine and super it must be extraordinarily delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastically' rearranges FINE, SUPER, SO and DL (the ends of 'delightful'); the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A jokey word for magnificent or marvellous, which fine, super and delightful all suggest.

clue.text: As part of time-sharing, taking turn in house

indicators.note: taking a turn means the found letters face the other way
the letters are found within the word time-sharing

explanation.surface: A timeshare arrangement where owners take turns in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: IMES sits inside 'time-sharing'; 'taking turn' reads it the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-detached house, shortened to semi in British usage, shares one wall with its neighbour.

clue.text: Horrify a mate, forgetting name for mountain area

parts.note: to appal is to horrify

indicators.note: forgetting the name means its letter is dropped

parts.note: china means mate, from Cockney rhyming slang china plate

explanation.surface: Someone horrifies a friend by forgetting the name of a mountain region.
explanation.walkthrough: CHIA is CHINA without N. Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a rhyming phrase, here 'china plate' for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of the eastern United States around the Appalachian Mountains goes by this name.

clue.text: Pensioner cycling by checkpoint made from shoddy material

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece is placed next to the other

parts.note: check is CH in chess notation, and a point of the compass gives E

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter from the front round to the back

parts.note: OAP stands for old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: An old man cycles past a checkpoint in a shoddily made outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' turns OAP into APO.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something cheap and poorly made is described this way.

clue.text: Out of power, allowed to be smutty?

parts.note: ex means out of or former
P is the physics symbol for power
licit means lawful or allowed

explanation.surface: Someone out of office asks whether they may now be smutty.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is one sense among several: graphic, not just clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphic sexual content is often labelled this way, so the word stands for smutty.

clue.text: Rest of Italian team's smutty, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard by a listener, so the spoken words give the answer

parts.note: Inter is the Milan football club, and lewd means smutty

explanation.surface: A rumour that the rest of an Italian side are vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: Inter Milan is a famous Italian football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or break between acts or periods of activity is a rest.

clue.text: Moving in Puck's direction, turned up on island, then left

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom, so back to front

parts.note: Puck is the setter, so towards Puck means towards me
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: Someone heads towards the setter, arrives on an island, then goes.
explanation.walkthrough: EMOT is 'to me' turned up. 'On' and 'then' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moving stirs the feelings, so a moving speech is a deeply felt one.

clue.text: Tory wearing light blue

indicators.note: the outer piece wears the inner one, so it goes around it

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
C stands for Conservative, the party of the Tories

explanation.surface: A Conservative dressed in pale blue, the party colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light blue' looks like one colour, but the definition is 'blue' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are risqué ones, so blue here means daring or suggestive.

clue.text: A Christian GP, say, covering 10

indicators.note: the doctor covers the other letters, so they go inside

parts.note: a GP is one kind of doctor, abbreviated DR
the digits one and zero look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A Christian family doctor looking after a particular patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' looks like a religion but is the fashion designer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian Dior was the French fashion designer, so one man named Christian is him.

clue.text: See 1
Remote possibility of bad luck

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad
chance means luck or fortune

explanation.surface: A slim prospect of misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight possibility that something might happen is known by this phrase.

clue.text: On the point of cupboard love

parts.note: a closet is a cupboard
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: On the verge of affection that is only for what is in the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Cupboard love is affection shown only to get something, like a pet fed from the cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nearly at a point is being on the point of it, as in near tears.

clue.text: See 7
Make former pupil tell story about the origin of greed

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: about means around, so the lie goes round the letter

parts.note: to tell a story is to lie

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Forcing an old boy to spin a tale about where greed comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone can mean to compel or force them, as does make.

clue.text: One performing unprepared, left holding a hole-boring tool? On the contrary

indicators.note: the holder has the other piece inside it
this reverses the stated roles, so the tool holds the letter, not the other way round

parts.note: a dibber is a pointed tool for making holes to plant seeds

explanation.surface: An improviser who left holding a gardening tool, or was it the reverse?
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' swaps who holds whom: L goes inside A DIBBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks or acts without preparation improvises, so they ad lib.

clue.text: Definitely happening — keep waiting to be connected

parts.note: an event that is on is going ahead
to hold is to keep

explanation.surface: A caller told it is definitely happening, then kept waiting on the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A caller parked by a switchboard is paused until put through, which is the phrase's telephone sense.

clue.text: Language coming from noisy party after stripper's act

indicators.note: once stripped, the word loses its outer layer, its first and last letters

parts.note: a shindig is a lively, noisy party

explanation.surface: Bad language heard at a rowdy party after a strip show.
explanation.walkthrough: SHINDIG stripped of its ends leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the main official language of India, so it is one example of a language.

clue.text: Abundance of fast sex between dessert and coffee, ultimately

indicators.note: the pieces sit between the two parts of the dessert

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, a dessert
Lent is the Christian season of fasting
it is a coy word for sex

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, the last letter of coffee

explanation.surface: A lavish dinner with a quick fling between pudding and coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: LENTIT goes inside PUD; 'ultimately' adds E from 'coffee'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty and abundance are synonyms, and this rarer form means the same.

clue.text: Sign new back for present season

indicators.note: going back means reading the letters in reverse order

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A sign for the new season, perhaps in a shop window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present season' is the season of presents.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas, the time of gift-giving, is a season of presents, and this is a French-derived word for it.

clue.text: Photographic chemical uncovering magic

parts.note: uncovering the word magic removes its outer letters, leaving the chemical symbols Ag and I

explanation.surface: A darkroom chemical reveals a kind of magic.
explanation.walkthrough: Ag is the symbol for silver and I for iodine, so AgI is the chemical formula of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This light-sensitive silver salt was used in early photographic plates and film.

clue.text: See 26
